items.prompt: The proposal, ___ merits are widely debated, was eventually adopted.

items.passage: Hi Sam, I am at the park with my dog. Come and meet us! The park is next to the school. — Lina
items.prompt: Where is Lina?

items.passage: SWIMMING POOL — Open every day 7am–9pm. Children under 8 must swim with an adult. Towels are not provided.
items.prompt: What must you bring to the pool?

items.passage: When Maya moved to a new city, she felt lonely at first. She joined a hiking club, and within a month she had made several friends. Now she says moving was the best decision she ever made.
items.prompt: How does Maya feel about moving now?

items.passage: Although remote work offers flexibility, many employees report that the boundary between their professional and personal lives has become blurred. Some companies now encourage staff to switch off notifications after working hours.
items.prompt: What problem does the text describe?
options: Work and private life mixing together

items.passage: Proponents of urban green spaces often emphasise their recreational value, yet the more compelling case may be economic: well-maintained parks have been associated with higher property values and reduced healthcare costs, benefits that accrue to the wider community rather than to park users alone.
items.prompt: According to the writer, the strongest argument for parks is that…
options: their benefits reach people beyond those who use them
they are popular places for recreation
they reduce the price of housing

items.passage: The historian’s account is meticulous in its detail but curiously reticent about causation; one finishes the book knowing precisely what occurred in each province, yet little the wiser as to why the rebellion erupted when and where it did.
items.prompt: The reviewer’s main criticism is that the book…
options: describes events without explaining their causes
is too short to be useful

items.passage: Tom gets up at six o’clock. He has breakfast, then he takes the train to work. He usually gets home at seven in the evening.
items.prompt: How does Tom go to work?

items.passage: The library will be closed for repairs from 3 to 17 March. During this time, books can be returned to the box outside the main entrance. Online services will continue as normal.
items.prompt: What can people do while the library is closed?

items.passage: Critics argued that the festival had become too commercial, with ticket prices out of reach for many local residents. Organisers responded by introducing discounted tickets for people living within ten kilometres of the venue.
items.prompt: Why did organisers introduce cheaper tickets?
options: To help local people afford them
To reduce the size of the crowd

items.passage: While the new curriculum was intended to foster critical thinking, teachers report that the volume of assessed content leaves little room for open-ended discussion, arguably undermining the very aim it was designed to achieve.
items.prompt: What does the writer suggest about the curriculum?
options: It works against its own goal
It has improved discussion in class
It reduced the amount of testing

items.passage: CAFÉ — Coffee £2. Tea £1.50. Cake £3. Open 8am to 5pm.
items.prompt: How much is a tea?

items.passage: To characterise the reforms as a capitulation would be to ignore the considerable concessions extracted from the opposition; yet to hail them as a triumph is equally to overlook how much of the original programme was quietly shelved.
items.prompt: The writer’s view of the reforms is that they were…
options: neither a clear defeat nor a clear victory

items.prompt: Where does Anna live?

items.script: The meeting is on Tuesday at three o’clock in room twelve.
items.prompt: When is the meeting?

items.script: I wanted to buy the blue jacket, but they only had it in a small size, so I bought the black one instead.
items.prompt: Which jacket did the speaker buy?

items.script: Sorry I’m late. The bus didn’t come, so I walked here. It took about forty minutes.
items.prompt: Why was the speaker late?

items.script: Our course normally costs two hundred pounds, but if you register before the end of the month, you’ll get a twenty per cent discount.
items.prompt: How can people pay less for the course?

items.script: I used to work in a bank, but I found it quite boring. Last year I retrained as a nurse, and although the hours are long, I find it much more rewarding.
items.prompt: How does the speaker feel about nursing?

items.script: The research suggests that people who take short breaks every hour are actually more productive than those who work without stopping, mainly because their concentration remains higher throughout the day.
items.prompt: Why are people who take breaks more productive?

items.script: We had originally planned to hold the conference in the city centre, but because of the rising cost of venues there, we’ve moved it to the university campus, which also has better transport links.
items.prompt: Why was the conference moved?
options: City centre venues became too expensive
The campus is in the city centre

items.script: What struck me most was not the scale of the project, impressive as it was, but the fact that the local community had been consulted at every stage, which is still surprisingly rare in developments of this kind.
items.prompt: What impressed the speaker most?

items.script: I’d hesitate to call the results disappointing; they fell short of our most optimistic projections, certainly, but they comfortably exceeded what most analysts had predicted.
items.prompt: How does the speaker view the results?

items.script: Far from settling the matter, the inquiry’s findings have, if anything, reopened questions that many had assumed were long since resolved, not least the extent to which officials were aware of the risks.
items.prompt: What effect did the inquiry have?

items.script: One could be forgiven for reading the author’s praise as sincere, though anyone familiar with her earlier essays will detect the unmistakable undertone of irony.
items.prompt: What does the speaker suggest about the author’s praise?
options: It was written by someone else
